In terrestrial burials, the casket would decompose, whereas a vessel does not. This may sound callous, but why does anyone care about a war grave of that nature other than purely sentimental reasons? For most burial sites, there is a secondary purpose in helping descendants to grieve and commemorate the deceased. I don't believe vessels in the middle of the ocean serve that purpose. There is likely a monument somewhere on land that fulfills that role much more effectively.

Practically speaking, the deceased don't care since they are no longer alive, and no descendants would visit the seafloor in the middle of the ocean anyway, making it a waste of a very valuable resource. I dislike it when people disturb gravesites solely because it is cheaper.
